subject: Logic
title: Zeno's Dichotomy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Zeno's Dichotomy.

hook.text: To walk across a room, you must first cross half. Then half of that. Then half again. You never arrive.

buildup.text: Zeno of Elea argued that motion requires completing infinite steps—which should be impossible.

discovery.text: Mathematically, 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ... actually sums to 1. Infinite steps can have a finite total.

twist.text: Zeno knew you could walk. His point was that our understanding of infinity was broken.

climax.text: Calculus eventually solved it. Infinite series converge—proving motion and infinity coexist.

quiz.question: What does Zeno's Dichotomy paradox challenge?
options: The possibility of motion through infinite steps
